plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 15.2.2
plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the partition construction used to define the line integral of a scalar function along a curve in 3D space. On the left, a curve from P = P0 to Q = Pn is divided into n arcs by partition points P1, P2, P3, ..., Pn-1, with the kth arc of length Delta_sk and mass Delta_Mk highlighted and a zoom arrow pointing to the right. On the right, the kth arc is isolated, spanning from P_{k-1} to Pk, with arc length Delta_sk labeled and the sampling point P*_k(x*_k, y*_k, z*_k) shown as a red dot on the arc. A formula box at the bottom reads Delta_Mk approx f(x*_k, y*_k, z*_k) Delta_sk. The figure introduces the Riemann sum approximation for the line integral by showing how the mass of each arc segment is approximated using the density value at a chosen sample point.

interactionPlan.concept: A line integral is defined by partitioning a curve into small segments, approximating the mass of each using a sample point, and summing these values; as the segments shrink, this Riemann sum converges to the exact integral.

Partition points P_0 through P_n drawn as blue dots on the main curve
Labels for points P=P_0, P_1, P_2, P_3, P_{k-1}, P_k, P_{n-1}, Q=P_n
Highlight or tick marks isolating the k-th arc segment on the main curve
Dimension lines and label for arc length \Delta s_k on the main curve
Text label 'Mass \Delta M_k' pointing to the k-th segment on the main curve

Magnified inset showing the k-th arc segment as a larger blue line
Points P_{k-1} and P_k as blue dots bounding the inset segment

interactions.label: Number of partitions (n)
interactions.teaches: Increasing the number of segments shrinks the length of each arc, refining the Riemann sum approximation towards the true continuous line integral.

interactions.label: Sample point position
interactions.teaches: Moving the sample point changes the evaluated density for a specific segment, but as segments become infinitesimally small, the exact placement within the segment ceases to affect the final sum.

demo_steps.title: Partitioning the curve
demo_steps.narration: The curve from P to Q is divided into n sub-arcs. We estimate the total mass by approximating the mass of each sub-arc and summing them.

demo_steps.title: Choosing a sample point
demo_steps.narration: Within each segment k, we pick a sample point to evaluate the density function. Slide the sample point position to see it move along the magnified arc segment.

demo_steps.title: Convergence
demo_steps.narration: As the number of partitions n approaches infinity, the length of each segment approaches zero, and the sum converges to the exact line integral regardless of sample point placement.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The exact line integral is found by breaking the curve into infinitely many pieces, where the sub-arcs become so small that the variation of the function within any single piece is negligible.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw the main curve as a smooth blue Bezier path with a distinctive loop. Distribute the partition points (blue dots) evenly along the curve based on the 'numSegments' slider. Keep the k-th segment visually anchored (e.g., around halfway along the path) so the zoom arrow always makes sense. The zoom arrow should be a thick, semi-transparent pale orange path with an arrowhead. In the magnified view, the red sample point's position along the blue arc segment is directly driven by the 'samplePos' slider (0 = P_{k-1}, 1 = P_k). Maintain math italicization for variables in the labels.

discrepancies: The main curve is drawn as a tangled path that intersects itself, whereas the source figure shows a simple, smooth spiral loop.
The large transition arrow from the main curve to the inset is awkwardly constructed with a misaligned and incorrectly rotated arrowhead.
A regex bug in the label logic causes numbered points to render with duplicate letters (e.g., 'PP₂' instead of 'P₂').
The dimension lines denoting Δsₖ lack the perpendicular extension bars present in the source.
The formula box is positioned at the top left (due to a positioning failure on the SVG group) rather than bottom center, and its text lacks proper math formatting.
The coordinates for the dynamic sample point label Pₖ*(xₖ*, yₖ*, zₖ*) overlap with the inset curve.
evaluation.notes: The interactivity is excellent, providing a pedagogically useful Riemann sum simulation with sliders and a step player, but the geometry and visual fidelity are extremely poor due to a malformed main curve, buggy label logic, and awkwardly drawn arrows.
action_items: Redraw the main curve path to form a clean, non-intersecting spiral loop.
Fix the transition arrow's geometry and arrowhead rotation so it smoothly maps the sub-arc to the inset.
Fix the label generation regex (e.g., changing the replacement logic) to prevent the 'PP₂' typo.
Use SVG transforms (.translate) instead of .move() on the formula box group to ensure it renders at the intended bottom-center position.
Add perpendicular extension lines to the ends of the dimension arcs for Δsₖ.
Use <tspan> elements with baseline-shift for proper mathematical subscripts and superscripts instead of relying on inline Unicode approximations.
